script: "That rude guest tried to book a room, but I exposed the killer secret…". I was clocking in at 3 pm during the annual youth science convention, and the front desk was a wreck. Three king rooms were still open, all standard. A call came in from a guy who'd booked through a third‑party site. He wanted to confirm a multi‑night stay, but the system said his reservation was cancelled—no explanation, just a "cancellation" flag from the third‑party. He was already mad, so I told him we only had standard kings left for the nights he wanted. He said he'd take it, so we booked him for two nights and I told him to call the third‑party to ask why it was cancelled. He didn't show up until the night‑audit shift. By the time he finally checked in, he was furious that his room only had one bed for his family of four. I told him that was what we had left and that he'd agreed to it. He demanded a roll‑away. Even though it violated fire code, the night‑audit staff obliged because it was late and I wasn't even there. Fast forward to the next day. I was already exhausted from the chaos of the night before, and my coworker was two hours late. I was about to lock in and start my shift when he stormed in at 6 pm, screaming that he wanted a better room and that we were a terrible hotel for not accommodating him the first night. I explained that we were fully booked for the next two nights and that we had no other rooms to offer. I apologized for the third‑party mishap, but he wouldn't accept it. He demanded a full refund for both nights. I told him we couldn't give a full refund because the cancellation was not our fault and that he had already agreed to the only room we had left. I offered to talk to my manager for a discount. My manager said, "Because of his behavior, we'll only give $50 off the two nights. If he keeps acting up, we'll ask him to leave." He was livid, demanding a full refund anyway. He stepped away for a moment, and I cried a little behind the counter—stress was real. He came back, yelling for a refund while I was busy checking in another guest. He wouldn't listen to any of the options I offered. I had had enough. I said, "We can't reach an agreement, and we're not meeting your expectations. This hotel isn't the right fit for you. I am canceling your second night. Pack your stuff and leave." He didn't take it well. I told him if he didn't leave, I'd call the police to escort him out. He shouted a big ol' "fuck you" and stormed off. About 30 minutes later, I watched him leave the building from behind the wall. I felt bad for his family, but his behavior was unacceptable and grounds for removal. He left the room a mess that I had to reset for the next guest. Lesson? Don't be an asshole to the people who have control over your reservation. The bestie, I am basically the only one who could have kept this from spiraling, but even I was out of options when he decided to act like a drama queen.
